summary:
Astronauts face unique physiological, psychological, and environmental health risks while becoming increasingly independent of Earth-based medical support. Communication delays during deep-space missions make autonomous healthcare capabilities essential. To address this challenge, we developed A.S.T.R.A., an AI-powered Flight Surgeon Companion designed to provide personalized health monitoring, medical decision support, and operational readiness assessments for astronauts.

A.S.T.R.A. integrates simulated wearable health data, clinical assessment algorithms, environmental monitoring, and conversational voice AI into a unified platform supporting EVA readiness screening, fatigue and cognitive performance assessments, and identification of concerning physiological trends and symptoms.

A.S.T.R.A. provides interactive, step-by-step medical guidance, enabling astronauts to independently measure vital signs, conduct basic laboratory assessments, and operate onboard diagnostic equipment.

By combining the aforementioned, A.S.T.R.A. supports proactive healthcare and informed decision-making during space missions. These capabilities could also improve terrestrial healthcare in remote and extreme environments, including polar research stations, offshore facilities, disaster response operations, and underserved communities with limited access to medical professionals.

The vision is to make reliable medical support more accessible, whether on Earth or millions of miles beyond it.
details:
A.S.T.R.A. is an autonomous clinical platform designed to support astronaut health, medical autonomy, and operational readiness during deep-space exploration missions, including Artemis lunar surface operations and future Mars transit missions.

As astronauts travel farther from Earth, communication delays, limited medical resources, and increasingly demanding mission environments create significant challenges for crew healthcare. A.S.T.R.A. addresses these challenges by integrating physiological monitoring, deterministic clinical assessment algorithms, environmental telemetry, and conversational artificial intelligence into a unified, crew-centered platform.

Serving as an AI Flight Surgeon Companion, A.S.T.R.A. goes beyond conventional health monitoring by helping astronauts understand their physiological status, recognize emerging medical concerns, independently perform guided medical procedures, and make informed decisions when immediate consultation with Earth-based flight surgeons is unavailable.

Key Capabilities

  • Clinical Assessment Engines: A.S.T.R.A. uses deterministic clinical scoring algorithms to evaluate astronaut health and operational readiness. Its EVA readiness assessments consider pressure-related risks, including barotrauma, cumulative radiation exposure from dosimetry, and joint mobility limitations that could impact spacesuit operations. Daily health assessments monitor physiological measurements and symptoms potentially associated with Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS), while the Fatigue Readiness module incorporates an in-browser psychomotor reaction-time test to help identify potential reductions in cognitive performance.
  • Hands-Free Conversational Voice AI: Recognizing that astronauts may have limited ability to interact with keyboards or touchscreens during certain mission activities, A.S.T.R.A. incorporates conversational voice capabilities using the Web Speech and Web Audio APIs. Crew members can verbally report symptoms, provide multiple health measurements in a single response, navigate guided medical checkups, and submit assessments through voice commands. Natural language processing (NLP) extracts relevant clinical information, while interactive visual feedback helps astronauts follow each step of the assessment.
  • NASA ARCHeR Wearable Actigraphy: A.S.T.R.A. simulates the ingestion of continuous physiological and activity data from NASA ARCHeR wearable technology, including photoplethysmography (PPG) and actigraphy measurements. The platform uses these data streams to evaluate sleep duration, sleep efficiency, cumulative sleep debt, and estimated sleep disruptions or micro-arousals. Interactive sleep-epoch visualizations, multi-day trend charts, and a real-time telemetry simulator allow astronauts to better understand how their sleep and recovery patterns evolve throughout a mission.
  • Mission & Environmental Profiling: Astronaut health cannot be evaluated independently of the environment and activities associated with a mission. A.S.T.R.A. incorporates a five-tab mission configuration workflow that captures mission parameters, spaceflight environmental conditions, Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) characteristics, and operational schedules. These inputs provide context for health assessments and enable automated pre-screening of potential concerns associated with upcoming activities, such as EVAs, or changes in the habitat environment.
  • Guided Clinical Protocols & Diagnostics: Beyond monitoring health data, A.S.T.R.A. is designed to help astronauts independently perform basic medical assessments when immediate support from an Earth-based flight surgeon is unavailable. The platform incorporates an interactive anatomical body map for documenting symptoms and provides step-by-step instructional guidance for obtaining vital signs, conducting basic laboratory assessments, and using onboard medical equipment. Guided protocols include ocular tonometry, pulse oximetry, orthostatic testing, and musculoskeletal ultrasound. These tools aim to reduce the burden on crew members while supporting consistent data collection, early identification of potential medical concerns, and communication with flight surgeons when further evaluation is required.

Future Development & Next Steps

Given additional development time, our team would focus on expanding A.S.T.R.A.'s predictive capabilities, improving the fidelity of its medical assessments, and further developing its conversational AI functionality.

  • Space Weather Integration: Integrate space weather forecasting APIs to monitor solar activity, identify potential solar energetic particle events, and provide early warnings of elevated radiation exposure risks. This would allow A.S.T.R.A. to incorporate predicted space weather conditions into mission planning and EVA readiness assessments.
  • Higher-Fidelity Radiation Modeling: Expand the current radiation assessment capabilities to incorporate more realistic radiation environments, including time-dependent exposure rates, cumulative mission dose, shielding characteristics, and astronaut-specific exposure histories. This would improve the platform's ability to evaluate radiation hazards across different mission phases and operational scenarios.
  • Enhanced Conversational AI: Continue refining A.S.T.R.A.'s voice agent to enable more natural, context-aware interactions with crew members. Improvements would include better recognition of medical terminology, more robust multi-turn conversations, and greater integration of individual health histories and mission conditions into its responses.
  • Expanded Medical Scenario Modeling and AI Training: Develop and inject a wider range of simulated medical and operational scenarios into the platform, including physiological changes, medical emergencies, environmental anomalies, and mission-related stressors. These scenarios would support iterative training, testing, and validation of A.S.T.R.A.'s AI capabilities, improving its ability to recognize emerging concerns, provide appropriate guidance, and respond consistently across a broader range of potential situations.

Together, these improvements would move A.S.T.R.A. toward a more comprehensive, predictive, and mission-aware autonomous clinical platform capable of supporting future exploration missions and remote healthcare applications on Earth.

Tools: Google Antigravity for vibe-coding

Tech Stack: Python/FastAPI, Vue.js/Nuxt.js, Docker (local development), Render for deployment.
